title: Unauthorised Possession and Disclosure of Information from HIV Registry
what_it_is: Unauthorised Possession and Disclosure of Information from HIV Registry

sections.label: Brochez arrest and HIV Registry data
sections.summary: Brochez was arrested in April 2016 for refusing a blood test and gave authorities 75 names from the HIV Registry, prompting a police report.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In late April 2016, Brochez was arrested for repeatedly refusing to comply with MOH's order to take a blood test.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: He then provided the Police and the Government authorities 75 names and particulars from the HIV Registry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This was the first time MOH had evidence that Brochez may have access to HIV-related data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We made a Police Report on 16 May 2016.

sections.label: Brochez retained disclosed data
sections.summary: Brochez retained at least the data he recently disclosed, and more cannot be ruled out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, as recent events showed, Brochez did manage to retain at least the data which he has recently disclosed, and we cannot rule out the possibility that he has more.

sections.label: AGC decision not to charge
sections.summary: AGC decided not to charge Brochez under the OSA because he would likely get only a fine or short jail term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: AGC decided not to charge him under the OSA because they assessed that he would likely be sentenced to a fine only, or, at most, a few weeks in jail.

sections.label: Brochez conviction and sentence
sections.summary: Brochez was convicted in March 2017 and sentenced to 28 months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Brochez was subsequently convicted in March 2017 and sentenced to 28 months' imprisonment.

sections.label: MOH decision against announcement
sections.summary: MOH judged that an announcement then would not serve affected individuals' interests against the anxiety and distress they would experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOH judged that, on balance, an announcement then would not serve the interests of the affected individuals, when weighed against the inevitable anxiety and distress they would experience.

sections.label: MOH contacting affected individuals
sections.summary: MOH decided to contact the affected individuals and alert them to the matter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOH, therefore, decided to contact the affected individuals and alert them to the matter.

sections.label: MOH public announcement decision
sections.summary: MOH decided to make a public announcement on 28 January despite concern about the impact on affected persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOH, therefore, decided to make a public announcement on 28 January, even though we remained deeply concerned about the impact this would have on the affected persons.

sections.label: MOH informing affected persons
sections.summary: At each juncture in May 2016, May 2018 and January 2019, MOH had to decide whether to inform affected persons and make a public announcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: At each juncture in May 2016, May 2018 and January 2019, MOH had to decide whether to inform the affected persons and make a public announcement.

sections.label: MOH managing further exposure
sections.summary: MOH decided to continue managing the situation in a way that reduces the possibility of further exposure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOH has decided to continue to manage the situation in a way that reduces the possibility of further exposure.

sections.label: Uploaded content and exposure
sections.summary: The uploaded content is similar to what was found in January, so no new individuals have been exposed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The content that was uploaded is similar to what we had found in January, so no new individuals have been exposed.

sections.label: Reached affected Singaporeans with HIV
sections.summary: Among affected Singaporeans diagnosed with HIV and still living, MOH has reached 2,400 out of 3,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Amongst the affected Singaporeans diagnosed with HIV and are still living, we have reached 2,400 out of 3,500.

sections.label: Employment laws and insurer assurance
sections.summary: MOM shared that Singapore has employment laws protecting employees from wrongful dismissals, including on HIV grounds, and LIA assured policyholders insurers will not use such information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOM shared that Singapore has employment laws to protect employees from wrongful dismissals, including on the grounds of HIV.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: LIA has, in turn, assured policyholders that insurers that receive information related to this incident will not use such information.

sections.label: Support for affected persons
sections.summary: They support affected persons, and the reactions were why no public announcement was made in 2016 and only affected patients were told in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, they do their best to support the affected persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These reactions are not unexpected and they were the reasons we made a judgement call in 2016 not to make a public announcement, and in 2018, to inform only the affected patients.

sections.label: Ler and HIV Registry
sections.summary: Ler, as Head of NPHU, had authority to access the HIV Registry and is believed to have downloaded it and lost possession; he was charged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As the Head of NPHU, Ler had authority to access information in the HIV Registry as required for his work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: He is believed to have downloaded the HIV Registry into a thumb drive and failed to retain possession of it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Ler has been charged for mishandling the information.

sections.label: Strengthened NPHU systems
sections.summary: Enhancements strengthened NPHU systems: higher approval authority, two-person approval, and a designated workstation for sensitive HIV Registry data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Following the review, enhancements were made to further strengthen the NPHU systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These include the following: (a) elevating the approval authority for downloading and decrypting Registry data to the level of the Director of our Communicable Diseases Division (CDD) or higher; (b) implementing a two-person approval process to download and decrypt Registry data, to ensure that data could not be accessed by a single person; and (c) designating a specific workstation for processing of sensitive data from the HIV Registry.

sections.label: HIV treatment and testing support
sections.summary: MAF gives means-tested subsidies covering up to 75% of anti-retroviral treatment, MediShield Life covers hospitalised persons with HIV, and anonymous testing is at 10 sites.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MAF provides means-tested subsidies for lower- and middle-income patients, covering up to 75% of the cost of anti-retroviral treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In 2015, with the introduction of MediShield Life, persons living with HIV are now covered by our national health insurance scheme should they be hospitalised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We have also made HIV testing and counselling services more widely available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, anonymous HIV testing is now available at 10 sites across the island.

sections.label: Workplace HIV guidelines
sections.summary: In 2017 SNEF, TTSH and HPB introduced guidelines on managing HIV and AIDS in the workplace to help companies create enabling environments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In 2017, the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF), Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH) and the Health Promotion Board (HPB) worked together to introduce "Guidelines on Managing HIV and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) in the Workplace" to help companies create enabling workplace environments for employees with HIV.

sections.label: Ler betrayed trust
sections.summary: Ler is a Singaporean doctor and ex-MOH officer entrusted with patient care who betrayed the trust of the Ministry and the medical profession.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Ler is a Singaporean doctor and ex-MOH officer who had been entrusted with the care of our patients, but he had betrayed the trust of the Ministry and the medical profession.

sections.label: Brochez HIV data breach act
sections.summary: Brochez, an American citizen, left a trail of lies and deceit and committed an act affecting thousands of persons with HIV.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The other, Brochez, is an American citizen who had left a trail of lies and deceit and now perpetrated a reprehensible act that has affected thousands of persons with HIV.

sections.label: Public disclosure of data breach
sections.summary: Public disclosure of the breach is a considered decision, with no standard timing applying to all data breach cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As to the issue of broader public disclosure of the breach, this is taken as a considered decision, taking into account the possibility that such a disclosure may allow the attacker to create more damage, may help him cover his tracks or may cause unnecessary distress.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Thus, there is no standard timing for public disclosure that automatically applies to all data breach cases.

sections.label: Disease environment and Singapore access
sections.summary: Long-term residents still face restrictions on access to Singapore, while restrictions for short-term stayers were recently lifted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We want to make sure that we are able to manage the disease environment here and to protect Singaporeans where possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, for persons with long-term residence in Singapore, we still have a restriction on their access to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For persons who are on short-term stay, the restriction has been lifted recently.

sections.label: Official Secrets Act offences
sections.summary: There could potentially be offences under the Official Secrets Act if further action is taken upon receipt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Technically, there could potentially be some offences under the Official Secrets Act, particularly if further action is taken upon receipt, to say, publicise it or send it to others.

sections.label: Anonymous HIV testing encouraged
sections.summary: Persons who suspect or are uncertain about HIV are encouraged to be tested, with identity kept anonymous and MOH receiving only aggregated numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: On the issue of HIV testing, we do encourage persons who suspect they may have HIV, or who are uncertain whether they have HIV, to come forward to be tested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The identity of the person will be kept anonymous and MOH will only receive an aggregated number of people who have tested.

sections.label: Public education to reduce HIV stigma
sections.summary: The Ministry will continue to step up public education efforts to reduce the stigma on HIV patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Ministry will also continue to step up efforts on public education to reduce the stigma on HIV patients.

sections.label: Structured support arrangements for people
sections.summary: The passage states efforts to work with and reach out to people needing support, and to formalise arrangements more structurally for sustainability and continuity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We try to work with them and see how we can best reach out to these people who need support and provide the relevant and effective support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will also look at how we can formalise these arrangements in a more structured way so that they are more sustainable and also, there is a continuity in the efforts.

sections.label: Reducing access to personalised data
sections.summary: The Member asks whether access to personalised data could be reduced to a minimum and split between individuals, with aggregated data used for policy analysis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In hindsight, I just wanted to ask the Minister, does the Minister feel there could be more scope going forward to maybe reduce the number of people who have access to the personalised data to the absolute minimum and possibly even break up access for the entire database between different individuals, so that very few, or perhaps even no individual, has access to all the personalised data, even though other individuals may have access to the aggregated data for the purpose of policy analysis?

sections.label: Data access on need-to-know basis
sections.summary: The passage states access to data has always been on a need-to-know and need-to-use basis, and NPHU staff numbers are very small.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: On the Member's question about access, in fact, access to the data has always been on a need-to-know and need-to-use basis, and the number of staff in NPHU is actually very small.

sections.label: Audit trail and access alerts
sections.summary: The new system has an audit trail, with alerts built in to flag excessive or unusual access to information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The new system that we put in place has audit trail and this audit trail was not meant to watch everybody and what they do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: There are certain alerts that are built into the system where if there are excessive access to the information, or where there is unusual kind of access to information, it will be flagged up.

sections.label: Deterrence and stern action
sections.summary: The passage states deterrence is important and stern action must be taken against illegal access, abuse or carelessness with entrusted information, as happened to Ler and Brochez.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The third level, which is equally important, and that is deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And that is why if we were to find someone who has made an illegal access or who has abused information or has been less than careful with the information that he is entrusted with, then we must take stern action and that is what happened to Ler and Brochez.

sections.label: Suicidal patients in calls
sections.summary: Medical social workers calling patients reported that some patients were suicidal and had to be managed delicately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, on the risk of suicidal tendencies, I get feedback from my medical social workers who are working on calling the patients and they do tell me that in their calls, there were patients who were suicidal and they have to manage the case very delicately.

sections.label: MOH audit compliance arrangements
sections.summary: The arrangements of the MOH team and involved officers were audited to be in compliance with the standards set.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the second point, the answer is yes, the arrangements that the MOH team and the officers who were involved in at the time were audited to be in compliance with the standards that were set.

sections.label: Backdating of sentence clarified
sections.summary: The sentence was backdated to the time he was first remanded, which was June 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On Mr Leon Perera's point earlier on the sentence, I would just like to clarify that it was backdated to the time that he was first remanded, which was June 2016.

sections.label: Expanding data governance division
sections.summary: The data governance division is being expanded to audit, visit and check ground operations and practices to ensure compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As I mentioned, we are now expanding the data governance division.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Currently, it is a very small unit and it is focusing on dealing with the policies, dealing with practices and reviewing MOH's governance practices on data security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But in order for them to do the audit function, to go down to the ground, to look at practices and to enforce practices, we would need to significantly enhance resources and these would include visiting and checking on the operations and practices on the ground to ensure compliance.

sections.label: Safeguards against database downloading
sections.summary: The speaker seeks confirmation that there was no safeguard against authorised staff downloading the entire database prior to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: You can access the database but why allow someone to download the entire database onto a thumb drive, to begin with?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I seek confirmation from the Minister that there was actually no safeguard against such downloading of the entire database by authorised staff prior to 2016.

sections.label: Delay in additional safeguards
sections.summary: The speaker asks why MOH took so long to implement additional safeguards, noting authorised staff could still download the entire database from 2013 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, why did it take so long for MOH to implement the additional safeguards because authorised staff still can access and download the entire database like what Ler did from 2013 to 2016, before the additional measures were put in?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have about 50, but the number who are looking at the governance division, we have about six.

sections.label: Portable storage devices requirement
sections.summary: Portable storage devices were allowed then, as encrypted storage devices were only required in 2017 under whole-of-Government policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: You were allowed to have portable storage devices at that time, because the encrypted storage devices were only a requirement in 2017, as a whole-of-Government policy, not MOH policy, but whole-of-Government.

sections.label: Civil action against MOH
sections.summary: Patients can take civil action against MOH for breach or loss of data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Patients can take civil action against MOH on breach of data or loss of data.

sections.label: Letters and demands motive
sections.summary: The motive for sending letters or demands is difficult to fathom, and no complaints of blackmail or threats have been received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, it is very difficult to fathom what is his motive in sending these letters or demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So far, we have not received any complaints or feedback on blackmails or threats from our patients or from any of our contacts.

sections.label: General policy on disclosure
sections.summary: A general Government policy on disclosure is asked about, but no single general rule exists due to complexities and the need to balance privacy and public interest.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I fear that without a general Government policy on the issue, the Government will find it difficult to effectively rebut claims or conspiracy theories about Government's lack of transparency.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Government if it would find elucidating, developing a general policy on disclosure useful to enhance transparency and public trust in the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As much as I would like to have a standard rule and say, "This is not my problem; I just follow the rules" —

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There are general guidelines for the handling of data, the training of officers, the protocols that should be in place across the public sector, including what are the considerations that should be taken into account after an incident occurs with respect to the affected individuals, the processes of the agency and the broader public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is quite a lot of thoughts, considerations and processes that are in place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But there is no single general rule, simply because of the complexities of the situations as we have described today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And as Members have heard from the difficulties in making the judgement call in this incident, you can imagine that it would be very, very difficult to come up with some general rule which will ultimately get the right balance between the privacy of the individual and the public interest, and we do want to strike that right balance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The other aspect to consider is that within the public sector, there are a number of other entities, Smart Nation and Digital Government Group, GovTech and also the security services and the Police where these matters can be reported to, and external views given by people who were not directly involved in the incident.
